Light boots since 10-22: a median of 62K (26 boots). The light boot of 00:22 on 11-16 took 90K with the held list read whole. The light boot of 13:32 took the context from 129K to 191K and read 44 of the held list's 420 lines (`C:16897`).
- The floor: the first call after a compaction already holds a median of 120K (93K to 138K): the summary, the system prompt, and what the harness re-attaches. The re-attached skills are 84K characters, about 29K tokens: the two project cores cut at 20K characters each, which the boot then loads again whole, and `update-config` and `artifact-design` at 20K characters each.
- After a full boot he sent a median of 8 messages before the next compaction (15 boots since 10-22); after a light boot, 17 (25 boots).
- A side finding: each load of the `fortress-repo` skill also attaches `Library/FlatString.fss` (6K characters), because the skill's text quotes a cache entry that starts `@"/home/user/fortress/Library/FlatString.fss"` and the harness reads that as a file mention (`C:13891`).

**Index.** `boot_cost.py --boot C:16094` and `--boot C:16815` print the two boots of today call by call with the context after each call.

**What it cannot show.** What each file in context is worth. Section 3 gives one number for it: corrections of kinds 1, 2 and 7 at 4.8 per 100 of his messages without FACTS and POSITIONS whole, against 1.0 with them.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Checks explorations/coordinator/INDEX.md against the tree: which standalone
# notes are missing a line, which lines name a file that is gone, which lines
# fall outside the set the index is meant to cover, and which paths named in a
# line's prose no longer resolve. Read-only. Exit 1 if the first two are
# non-empty.
#
# The note set is every *.md under explorations/ except run/experiment trees
# (which document themselves in their own README) and evidence directories.
# Edit the two lists below when the shape of the tree changes.

set -uo pipefail

root=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)
index="$root/explorations/coordinator/INDEX.md"
[ -f "$index" ] || { echo "no INDEX.md at $index" >&2; exit 2; }

# Run/experiment trees: a directory holding one run's sources and evidence.
run_roots='apl|astra|blinded-fable|compile-ladder|run-b|run-b2|run-c|run-c3|run-c4|fortify|ci|experiment'
# Generic evidence directory names, at any depth.
evidence_dirs='probes|checks|goldens|figures|evidence|measurements|raw|src|tools|gate|cold-cache|reference|archive|build|article|worker|notes|recovered-reports|_prior|__pycache__|existing-tests|failed|png|regen|tic-regen|tour|pairs|combos'

notes=$(cd "$root" && find explorations -name '*.md' \
  | grep -vE "(^|/)[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+-(probes|pairs)/" \
  | grep -vE "(^|/)($evidence_dirs)/" \
  | grep -vE "^explorations/($run_roots)/" \
  | grep -v '^explorations/coordinator/INDEX.md$' \
  | sort)

# Entry keys: the backticked path at the start of an index bullet.
keys=$(grep -oP '^- `\K[^`]+' "$index" | sort -u)
# Entry keys that are notes (drop the .js/.sh entries from the comparison set).
key_notes=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | grep '\.md$' | sort -u)

missing=$(comm -23 <(printf '%s\n' "$notes") <(printf '%s\n' "$key_notes"))
stale=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | while read -r p; do
  [ -n "$p" ] && [ ! -e "$root/$p" ] && echo "$p"
done)
outside=$(comm -13 <(printf '%s\n' "$notes") <(printf '%s\n' "$key_notes"))

tracked=$(mktemp); trap 'rm -f "$tracked"' EXIT
(cd "$root" && git ls-files) > "$tracked" 2>/dev/null || : > "$tracked"

# Paths named inside a line's prose (not the entry key) that resolve nowhere.
dangling=$(grep -oP '`\K[^`]{1,120}?\.(md|js|sh|py|fss|fsi|html|tic|svg|csv|tsv|txt|yml)(?=`)' "$index" \
  | grep '/' | grep -v '[[:space:]]' | sort -u | while read -r p; do
    if [ -e "$root/$p" ] || [ -e "$root/explorations/$p" ] \
       || [ -e "$root/explorations/coordinator/$p" ]; then continue; fi
    # last resort: the reference may be relative to a directory deeper in the tree
    grep -q "/$p\$" "$tracked" || echo "$p"
  done)

n() { [ -z "$1" ] && echo 0 || printf '%s\n' "$1" | wc -l | tr -d ' '; }

echo "INDEX.md check — $(cd "$root" && git rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo 'no git')"
echo "notes in scope: $(n "$notes")   index entries: $(n "$keys")"
echo
echo "== notes missing from INDEX.md ($(n "$missing")) =="
[ -n "$missing" ] && printf '%s\n' "$missing"
echo
echo "== index lines naming a file that does not exist ($(n "$stale")) =="
[ -n "$stale" ] && printf '%s\n' "$stale"
echo
echo "== index lines outside the note set, informational ($(n "$outside")) =="
[ -n "$outside" ] && printf '%s\n' "$outside"
echo
echo "== paths named in a line's prose that resolve nowhere ($(n "$dangling")) =="
[ -n "$dangling" ] && printf '%s\n' "$dangling"

[ -n "$missing" ] || [ -n "$stale" ] && exit 1
exit 0

#!/bin/bash
# Switches the workflow scripts and the headless writers between the two tier settings:
#   regular  the tiers of the coordinator skill's references/delegating.md (Opus workers, Sonnet scouts,
#            Fable for a judge's second ruling), and the headless writers on Opus;
#   fable    every agent on Fable, at medium effort where it ran on Opus and at low effort where it ran
#            on Sonnet, and the headless writers on Fable at medium effort.
# It edits the one switch line of each file (FABLE_WEEK in the three workflow scripts, WRITER_MODEL and
# WRITER_EFFORT in tiers.sh), checks the batch script, and commits nothing.
#
#   tier-mode.sh status     print the setting of each file
#   tier-mode.sh fable      set every file to the Fable setting
#   tier-mode.sh regular    set every file to the regular setting
#
# Do not switch while a workflow runs: a resume needs the script as launched (the coordinator skill's
# references/delegating.md, "Interrupts and process stops"). After a switch: commit the four files by name.
# The tier of an Agent-tool worker is not set here: the coordinator names it in each launch.
set -euo pipefail
here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
scripts=("$here/../climb-batch-workflow.js" "$here/record-landing/record-landing.js" "$here/orientation/orientation.js")
tiers="$here/tiers.sh"

status() {
  for f in "${scripts[@]}"; do
    n=$(grep -c '^const FABLE_WEEK = \(true\|false\)$' "$f" || true)
    [ "$n" = 1 ] || { echo "tier-mode: $f has $n switch lines, expected 1" >&2; exit 1; }
    v=$(sed -n 's/^const FABLE_WEEK = \(true\|false\)$/\1/p' "$f")
    printf '%-8s %s\n' "$([ "$v" = true ] && echo fable || echo regular)" "${f#"$here"/}"
  done
  # shellcheck disable=SC1090
  ( . "$tiers"; printf '%-8s %s (WRITER_MODEL=%s WRITER_EFFORT=%s)\n' \
      "$([ "$WRITER_MODEL" = fable ] && echo fable || echo regular)" "tiers.sh" "$WRITER_MODEL" "${WRITER_EFFORT:-}" )
}

set_mode() {
  local flag=$1 model=$2 effort=$3
  status >/dev/null
  for f in "${scripts[@]}"; do
    sed -i "s/^const FABLE_WEEK = \(true\|false\)$/const FABLE_WEEK = $flag/" "$f"
  done
  sed -i "s/^WRITER_MODEL=.*$/WRITER_MODEL=$model/; s/^WRITER_EFFORT=.*$/WRITER_EFFORT=$effort/" "$tiers"
  status
  if [ -f "$here/workflow-scenarios.js" ]; then
    echo "--- the batch script's scenario check:"
    node "$here/workflow-scenarios.js" 2>&1 | tail -3
  fi
  echo "--- commit by name: ${scripts[*]#"$here"/} tiers.sh"
}

case "${1:-status}" in
  status)  status ;;

Until then, state neither side as right, and take no step that rests on the point until the recheck ends.

- Run an Opus worker that writes or condenses a long report at extra high effort, `xhigh`: the Agent tool's `effort` option, `agent()`'s `opts.effort`, or `--effort xhigh` on a headless session's command line.

Fable writes no text that goes as written into the record, since its compressed register degrades the reasoning. A Fable worker may give corrections to a text that Opus writes, and Opus words them into the text. A Fable review may edit a batch record in place.

# Drafts that wait for the curator's yes, 2026-11-16

Each draft changes `.claude/skills/coordinator/SKILL.md`. None has landed.

## Draft A: the register of every message to the curator

Section "Talking to the curator", the first bullet.

Current text:

> - Write plain short sentences, with contractions, halfway to ASD-STE100: active voice, one word for one thing. Keep replies brief.

Proposed text:

> - Write in the register of ASD-STE100: short sentences, active voice, one word for one thing, no contractions. Keep replies brief.

Note. The current bullet asks for contractions and for a register halfway to ASD-STE100. The curator's order at 15:35 UTC on 2026-11-16 was: "Try again presenting the results of the analysis. Go to register of ASD-STE100." The proposed bullet asks for that register in full, with no contractions. The order named one presentation. That it holds for every message is the coordinator's reading, not the curator's words. The third bullet of the section already says to define each term where it is used, so the proposed bullet does not repeat that. The bullet is about the same length as before.

## Draft B: a default does not replace the curator's reading

Section "Talking to the curator", "An ask", the last paragraph, its first sentence. To pay for the added words, the draft also cuts a repeated definition from the paragraph before it.

Current text:

> Give each decision a default that the curator can take without reading the argument. Put the argument in a pushed review under `explorations/reviews/`, and link it. Offer no option that does nothing.

Proposed text:

> Give each decision a default, so that the work does not wait. Never tell the curator to take it unread: each ask is how the curator learns what changed in the tree. Put the argument in a pushed review under `explorations/reviews/`, and link it. Offer no option that does nothing.

Current text of the sentence that pays for it:

> Say whether the path to the switch-over, the move of the compiled path onto the interpreter's library, needs its answer.

Proposed text:

> Say whether the path to the switch-over needs its answer.

Note. The current sentence says that the curator can take a default without reading. The coordinator used it to put ten design decisions as defaults to take. The curator objected at about 18:2x UTC on 2026-11-03: he rarely sees the Fortress source that the workers change, so each decision is his chance to learn what changed, and a default taken unread widens that gap. The proposed text keeps the default, gives its one purpose, which is that the work does not wait, and tells the coordinator to inform the curator on each decision. The cut words define the switch-over a second time: the glossary's entry for PLAN already defines it. The two changes together make the section about 5 characters shorter.

## Draft C: a review of a subject as a whole

Section "Talking to the curator", "An ask", the opening sentence.

Current text:

> **An ask.** Put decisions one at a time, one ask in a message, in this order:

Proposed text:

> **An ask.** Put decisions one at a time, one ask in a message. If the curator asks for a review of a subject as a whole, give one picture of the subject with its forks, not one ask for each item. An ask goes in this order:

Note. The current rule puts every decision alone. On 2026-11-08, at about 14:2x UTC, the curator had asked for one review of literals as a whole, since he saw the same shape in string literals, float numerals and integer numerals. The coordinator sent three separate asks, each with its own list of fixes, and the curator objected. The proposed sentence is the exception to "one at a time". One sentence holds the rule, but it makes the section about 140 characters longer, and this draft names no cut that pays for it.

# Report

Part 1 is committed as `8b16560989`, not pushed. Part 2 is drafted in `tmp/skill-writer/drafts-postmortem-2026-11-16.md`, uncommitted. The lint is clean on the three files.

I could not run `check-index.sh`: the shell's permission check refused it three times. I kept step 2 from a reading of the script's source, so that choice is untested.

## Sizes

- `SKILL.md`: 33,735 before, 33,731 after.
- `references/delegating.md`: 12,087 before, 12,086 after.
- `references/sources.md`: one new section of eight lines.

## "The boot", new text

The paragraphs "The transcript backup" and the model check's bullet are unchanged except where noted below, so I give them in short.

> At session start and after each compaction, take these steps in order. If the curator names another form of the boot, that word replaces these steps and the hook's list of files.
>
> 0. (unchanged: the model, then the transcript backup)
> 1. `POSITIONS.md`, whole. Read it in pages: it is larger than one page of the Read tool.
> 2. Run `explorations/coordinator/check-index.sh`. Add an INDEX line for each note that it reports.
> 3. `PLAN.md`, its first section.
> 4. The boot note, then the held list.
> 5. `git log --oneline -15`, for a worker's commit newer than the boot note.
> 6. If the boot note says that a batch runs, load `references/batch.md` and read what its "While it runs" names. Say nothing about the batch before that.
> 7. Load `references/delegating.md`, `references/record.md` and `fortress-repo`'s `references/records.md`, so that you give the work to workers and keep the record by its rules.
> 8. (unchanged: the calibration check)
>
> `FACTS.md` and `INDEX.md` stay unread. Before you state a fact, or put anything to the curator, search them with `facts-extract.sh`. Read only FACTS whole, and only at a batch landing:
>
> 1. At the first batch landing after the boot, read `FACTS.md` whole, in pages. Do it before step 1 of `references/batch.md`, "The landing". If the boot falls inside a batch landing, after step 1 of "The landing", read it at once, before the next step.
> 2. When the record-landing workflow of step 4 of "The landing" ends, read what it changed in FACTS and POSITIONS.
> 3. At a later batch landing before the next compaction, read only what it changed in the two files.
>
> **The full boot.** Only at the curator's word, read `FACTS.md` and `INDEX.md` whole too, after step 1. It costs about three times the context. After it, skip step 1 of the list above.
>
> **After a compaction,** a copy of a skill or a part that the harness shows from before it counts as not loaded: it can be cut or old. Load each skill's core with the Skill tool, and read each part from disk before its work.
>
> **The transcript backup.** Check it at every boot and after every VM restart, since the backup fails with no message: (three bullets unchanged)
>
> A batch landing's work never waits for a compaction or a boot, and you ask the curator nothing about the boot.
>
> - Read nothing that the boot does not name. List no directory, and bound every command's output.
> - To learn whether a worker runs, read the harness's notice at the top of the turn. After an interrupt or a process stop, check each worker's state, and that each output file is complete, not only that it exists, before you say what ran or was lost. Relaunch a killed worker only as `references/delegating.md`, "Interrupts and process stops", says.
> - Rewrite the boot note whole at every change. Never append to it.
> - (unchanged: the model check's alarm)

The merged boot text is shorter than the old steps plus "A light boot". With the two new rules, the whole section is about 36 characters longer than before. The file is not longer, because the cut in "The standing goal" pays for it.

## Other changed sentences

- `SKILL.md`, "The standing goal": "Read a worker's final message yourself." is cut.
- `delegating.md`, "Which tier runs what", new bullet: "`explorations/coordinator/tools/tier-mode.sh` (`status`, `fable`, `regular`) switches the workflow scripts and the headless writers between these tiers and Fable for every agent. Run it only while no workflow runs."
- The same section, shortened to pay for the bullet, with no rule changed:
  - "Name each worker's tier by its alias only: `model: 'opus'`, `'sonnet'` or `'fable'`."
  - "Use Sonnet only for archaeology and to fetch exact words."
  - "Until the recheck ends, state neither side as right, and take no step that rests on the point."
  - "… at `xhigh` effort: … or `--effort xhigh` for a headless session."
  - "`explorations/coordinator/tools/model-now.sh` prints a Fable session's version."
  - "For a cross-area question, Opus workers first gather cited evidence or a list of ways."
  - "Without it, its prompts read as the curator's messages in your own transcript."
  - "Today only the baseline interview does so." is cut.

No cross-reference to "A light boot" stands in another skill file, so none was changed.

## Part 2 drafts

- **Draft A (item 6):** "Write in the register of ASD-STE100: short sentences, active voice, one word for one thing, no contractions. Keep replies brief." The note says that the reach to every message is the coordinator's reading.
- **Draft B (item 7):** "Give each decision a default, so that the work does not wait. Never tell the curator to take it unread: each ask is how the curator learns what changed in the tree." It also cuts the second definition of the switch-over from the paragraph before. The section still grows by about 20 characters.
- **Draft C (item 8):** one sentence holds the rule: "If the curator asks for a review of a subject as a whole, give one picture of the subject with its forks, not one ask for each item." It grows the section by about 150 characters, and I found no cut to pay for it.

## Decisions not taken

- **The tier switch against the writer rule.** `tier-mode.sh fable` puts the headless writers on Fable, but the section still says "Run every writer on Opus … also when this session runs on Fable". The alternatives are to leave both, to add "except under the Fable setting" to the writer rule, or to drop the writers from the switch.
- **"While Fable is at version 5.1".** The session now runs on Fable 5.2, so the rules on Fable's text may have lapsed by their own words. The alternatives are to keep the bound, to raise it, or to remove it.
- **The reason for FACTS at a landing.** I cut "Naming the decisions that landed and planning the batch after it need both files whole" for length. The alternative is to restore it for FACTS and cut about 85 characters elsewhere.
- **`record.md` line 73** says "before the next boot or batch reads FACTS". The default boot no longer reads FACTS. I left it, because it is still true of the full boot.
- **Step 2, `check-index.sh`.** If its output proves long at a boot, the alternatives are to bound it to its first list or to move it to the batch landing.

## What I could not follow

- The compaction hook's message in `.claude/settings.json` still lists FACTS and INDEX whole. Until you change it, it is a closed list that contradicts the section.
- The sources lines for the choices that were mine to settle say "settled by the skill writer", which is not one of the three source names that the standing brief allows.

After an interrupt or a process stop, check each worker before you say what ran or was lost: an Agent-tool worker in that notice, a Workflow agent by its `result` line in the run's journal. - "`explorations/coordinator/tools/tier-mode.sh fable` puts every agent of the workflow scripts and the headless writers on Fable. `regular` puts them back on this section's tiers, and `status` prints the setting. Switch only at the curator's word, and only while no workflow runs. Under the `fable` setting every worker runs on Fable, and this section's rules on which tier runs what do not apply."
- "The rules on Fable's text hold while Fable is at version 5.1. `explorations/coordinator/tools/model-now.sh` prints this session's model."

The character counts in the drafts' notes are my estimates, not measured.

# Task: six held points of the curator for the `fortress-repo` skill

These are points that the curator, Pavol, raised and that wait for this skill. Each is small. Make each change in the fewest words, and make no file longer: where a point adds a sentence, cut as many characters from text of the same section that states no rule. `references/compiler.md` is at its limit and `references/revival-changes.md` is over its budget, so those two must end shorter than they are, or equal. Check each claim about the tree against the tree before you write it; if a point's ground is wrong, change nothing for it and say so in your report. One commit; do not push. A cold read follows.

1. **A probe's patch and report are committed.** `references/committing.md` defines scratch as "logs, captured and raw run output, copies of tools, probe programs, lists and private caches folders", and `SKILL.md`, "Rules for every task", says "Do not commit scratch: logs, captured output, probe programs." The curator's correction of 19:3x UTC on 2026-11-08, when the coordinator told a probe's worker to commit nothing: a probe's exploration is committed, its patch and its report, "as others were" (`explorations/compile-ladder/plan-19/probes/*.patch` and the later plans' `probes/` folders show the practice); only the code stays off `main` until a rung lands it test first. Say where a probe's patch, report and programs go: the plan's `probes/` folder, committed; logs and captured output stay scratch. Bring `committing.md`, the rule in `SKILL.md` and `references/exploring.md` in line, each in its own words, with one home for the rule and pointers from the others.
2. **A test case is in one file only.** `references/tests-writing.md`. The curator, 18:1x UTC on 2026-11-10, on numeral cases that a new test repeated from the team's test: "I don't want the same test case in several files. That's wrong." The rule: before a worker adds a case, it looks for the test that already holds cases of its kind, and adds the case there; a case that a test already asserts is not asserted again in another file.
3. **An assertion's message is one short line.** `references/tests-writing.md`. The curator, 17:5x UTC on 2026-11-10, on messages of two lines in the round-trip numeral tests: "can't you write something leaner? Who wants to read an error message from two lines? Let's keep it simple." The rule: an assertion's message says what was checked in one short line; a reason that several assertions share goes in one comment line above them.
4. **`references/tests-writing.md`, the sentence "An `XXX` test with such a `.test` file is green if the program loads and runs clean."** (the bullet on a refusal at load). On 2026-10-09 it read to the curator as a warning that the inversion of an `XXX` test does not apply here. It does apply. Say what such a test records, a refusal that walk misses, and that it turns red when the fix makes walk refuse; keep the plain case and the `XXX` case apart, and keep what the bullet says on the promotion (the rename of both files and of the component).
5. **`references/library.md`, "Designing a change", two sentences.**
   - "Put each extension into this library, outside the compiler's files. This includes an extension that only the model program needs." The curator said on 2026-10-09 that this contradicts his position. His position is now the record's entry P-27 (`explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh 'P-27'`): what a program builds that a more mature library would hold goes into the library, in the library's own way; a form that the library has for one number type, rank or sibling trait and lacks for another is the plainest case; a form that extends the program's own domain stays in the program. State that rule, as the tree holds it, without naming the entry as its source in the text.
   - "follow the team's proposal, which no program can import (`Library/incomplete/Collection.fss`)" reads strangely to him. He understands that the folder is imported nowhere; he suggested "follow the team's unfinished collection design".
6. **Two sentences that the record has made false.**
   - `references/compiler.md`, "The compiler's prelude, until the switch-over": where it says that the numerals are the one exception to the rule that no declaration is added to the compiler's prelude, there are now two: the numerals, and the built-in number types, which take the form of one `value object` each on both paths before the switch-over (P-37 and P-178: `facts-extract.sh 'P-37'`, `'P-178'`). Check what the section says today, and bring it in line only if it is false.
   - `references/revival-changes.md`, the rule "Write every parameter type." (about line 134): it says that the compiled path refuses a parameter without a type. Read ledger rows 1032 and 405 and the entries F-370 and F-371 (`facts-extract.sh 'ledger:1032'`, `'F-370'`, `'F-371'`), and bring the sentence in line with what they establish about a component's function whose api declares the types. If the sentence is already true, leave it.

## How to work

- Read each part whole before you edit it. `git grep` for each sentence that you move, so that no cross-reference breaks.
- Add one line for each change to `references/sources.md` of `fortress-repo`.
- Run the skills' lint on each file that you change.
- Report: each changed sentence, new text only, with its file and section; each file's size before and after; the points that you left unchanged, with the reason; the decisions that you did not take.

# Committing and pushing

**scratch**
: Files and folders that your work makes and `main` does not keep: logs, captured and raw run output, copies of tools, probe programs, lists and private caches folders.

Your brief says whether you commit and push, and on which branch. If it says nothing, commit on your current branch, and push it.

## What to commit

- Commit your change, its tests, your report if it is a file, and any reusable script.
- Commit what you write to the record, such as a ledger row, with the work that it records. A row's close follows the fix's commit (`records.md`).
- Keep scratch in your tree's `tmp/`, which is gitignored.
- In a fresh clone, `.claude/worktrees/` and `.claude/agents/` show as untracked, because the lines of `.git/info/exclude` that hide them are not in the clone. Do not commit them.
- Keep a copyrighted PDF or deck in `research/decks/`, which is gitignored. Cite it by its Wayback URL. Notes on it go in `research/extracts/`: your own summary, with brief attributed quotations.
- Put provenance and rationale in commit messages and reports, not in source comments.
- Name a model by its tier (Opus, Sonnet, Fable) in any text that you commit, commit messages included. Never write its model identifier, the API's name for the model, which starts with `claude-`.

## How to commit

Commit as you go, each commit in one command that names its paths:

    git add -- <paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <paths>

- The command commits only the paths that it names. Other agents may have uncommitted edits in your tree. Leave them alone.
- If you renamed a file with `git mv`, name its old path in `git commit` only, because `git add` refuses a path that no longer exists: `git add -- <new paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <new paths> <old paths>`.
- Never commit a copied directory, and never use `git add -A`.
- Before you commit more than a few hundred lines, stage them and read what you staged: `git add -- <paths> && git diff --cached --stat -- <paths>`.
- If the commit edits the original tree, say so in its message.
- End every commit message with this footer, exactly, whatever footer Claude Code suggests:

      Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
      Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AmiXNpJxQ6TBwec4vJZHDB

  If your brief gives another session line, use it. If a commit that is already made has a footer that names a model, by any name or identifier, leave the commit as it is. Such a footer is not a defect: do not check for it, report it or list it.

## Pushing

Push after every commit, so that a lost container loses nothing.

- If you work on your own branch, push it: `git push -u origin <branch>` the first time, then `git push`. Your brief says how the branch reaches `main`.
- From a session in a cloud container, do not try to delete a branch on GitHub, or retry a refusal with another tool (the `cloud-container` skill, "Rules for every agent"). Removing a worktree does not delete its branch, which stays. Ask nobody in your report to delete a branch.
- If you work on `main`, other agents commit to it too. Push only your own commits:
  1. Run `git log origin/main..main`. Your commits are those whose hashes your own `git commit` printed.
  2. If it lists another agent's commit, run the command again shortly: that agent pushes right after it commits. If the commit stays, push nothing, and say so in your report.
  3. If it lists only your commits, push the three refs with this one command, and wait for it to end:

         git push --atomic origin main main:claude/worker-brief-fable-vnnuv8 main:blinded-fable

     With `--atomic`, the three refs update together or not at all. Do not pipe the command into another command, since a pipe hides a refusal. A refusal shows as a line that starts with `!`, and as a non-zero exit. The last ref keeps `blinded-fable` current. If the container is lost, the platform rebuilds it from that branch.
- Push no branch that this section does not name, unless your brief names it.

1	# Writing a test
2	
3	**gated test**
4	: Test that the gate's suites run.
5	
6	**green**
7	: Harness's report on a test that JUnit counts as passed.
8	
9	**red**
10	: Harness's report on a test that JUnit counts as failed.
11	
12	**`XXX` test**
13	: Gated expected failure. It asserts the answer that the specification gives, and fails today. The harness reports it green while it fails, and red when the defect is fixed.
14	
15	## A test program
16	
17	A test program has this form:
18	
19	    component Name
20	    export Executable
21	
22	    (* declarations *)
23	
24	    run(): () = do
25	        assert(f(2), 4, "f(2)")
26	    end
27	
28	    end
29	
30	- `(*)` starts a comment to the end of the line. It cannot hold `*)`: the parser ends the comment there and refuses the program. `(* ... *)` comments nest.
31	- A compiled test with a `run` key ends `run()` with `println("PASS")`, unless a `run_out` key checks its output (below).
32	- Under walk, `assert(x, y, msg)` checks that `x` equals `y`. It and `=/=` call a type's own `=` only if the type extends a `FortressLibrary` trait that declares `=`, such as `Equality` (ledger row 807). Otherwise they compare by `SEQV` (`revival-changes.md`, "Traits and objects"). If a type `P` has its own `=`, make `P` extend `Equality[\P\]`, or write `assert(x = y, msg)`. The compiler's library declares the two-value `assert` only for `ZZ32`, `String` and `Character`; its `assert(flag, msg)` takes any `Boolean`.
33	- Do not name a variable or a parameter after a functional method of the library, such as `big`, `even`, `numerator` or `shift`. The disambiguator, the phase that binds names, refuses it: "Variable even is already declared."
34	- A superscript is `^` and what follows it, as the exponent in `x^2` or the transpose `^T`. It can follow a dotted access: `p.wq^T` is `(p.wq)^T`. After a call or a subscript, parenthesise first, as `(f(x))^T` and `(x[5])^2`: `f(x)^T` is a static error, and `x[5]^2` stops the compile, and under walk fails or gives the wrong element (ledger rows 1005 and 1).
35	- A test of run-time arithmetic or concatenation needs a variable operand, not a literal, because an expression of literals alone folds before the run (`revival-changes.md`, "Numbers").
36	
37	## Where a test goes, and how it passes
38	
39	Interpreter (walk): write `ProjectFortress/tests/Name.fss`, whose component is `Name`.
40	
41	- Every `.fss` file there is gated, with no `.test` file needed.
42	- It is green if it throws no exception, exits 0, and neither its standard output nor its standard error contains `fail` or `FAIL`. A longer word counts too: `failure` fails the test. Only a file whose name contains `QuickCheckTest` is exempt.
43	- An api that it imports, and a helper component, go in `ProjectFortress/test_library/`. In `tests/`, a helper would run as a test.
44	- The harness skips files whose names end in `Syntax.fss`, `DynamicSemantics.fss` or `Satisfiability.fss`, or contain `GenomeUtil`.
45	- For a refusal at load, put `Name.test` beside `tests/Name.fss`, with `load_exception_contains=<message>`. A plain test is green if walk refuses the program at load as named. A failure while the top-level variables are initialised counts as a refusal. An `XXX` test with such a `.test` file is green if the program loads and runs clean.
46	
47	Compiled: write `Name.fss` and `Name.test` in the compiled test folder that holds tests of its kind:
48	
49	- `library_tests/`: the compiler's library. A test of the interpreter's library is an interpreter test (above).
50	- `parser_tests/`: the parser.
51	- `compiler_tests/`: the rest, beside the team's numbered `CompiledN` tests.
52	- `other_compiler_tests/`: the team's compiled tests that do not fit the `CompiledN` series, by the comment in `OtherCompilerJUTest.java`. Put no new test there.

# Writing a test

**gated test**
: Test that the gate's suites run.

**green**
: Harness's report on a test that JUnit counts as passed.

**red**
: Harness's report on a test that JUnit counts as failed.

**`XXX` test**
: Gated expected failure. It asserts the answer that the specification gives, and fails today. The harness reports it green while it fails, and red when the defect is fixed.

## A test program

A test program has this form:

    component Name
    export Executable

    (* declarations *)

    run(): () = do
        assert(f(2), 4, "f(2)")
    end

    end

- `(*)` starts a comment to the end of the line. It cannot hold `*)`: the parser ends the comment there and refuses the program. `(* ... *)` comments nest.
- A compiled test with a `run` key ends `run()` with `println("PASS")`, unless a `run_out` key checks its output (below).
- Under walk, `assert(x, y, msg)` checks that `x` equals `y`. It and `=/=` call a type's own `=` only if the type extends a `FortressLibrary` trait that declares `=`, such as `Equality` (ledger row 807). Otherwise they compare by `SEQV` (`revival-changes.md`, "Traits and objects"). If a type `P` has its own `=`, make `P` extend `Equality[\P\]`, or write `assert(x = y, msg)`. The compiler's library declares the two-value `assert` only for `ZZ32`, `String` and `Character`; its `assert(flag, msg)` takes any `Boolean`.
- Do not name a variable or a parameter after a functional method of the library, such as `big`, `even`, `numerator` or `shift`. The disambiguator, the phase that binds names, refuses it: "Variable even is already declared."
- A superscript is `^` and what follows it, as the exponent in `x^2` or the transpose `^T`. It can follow a dotted access: `p.wq^T` is `(p.wq)^T`. After a call or a subscript, parenthesise first, as `(f(x))^T` and `(x[5])^2`: `f(x)^T` is a static error, and `x[5]^2` stops the compile, and under walk fails or gives the wrong element (ledger rows 1005 and 1).
- A test of run-time arithmetic or concatenation needs a variable operand, not a literal, because an expression of literals alone folds before the run (`revival-changes.md`, "Numbers").

## Where a test goes, and how it passes

Interpreter (walk): write `ProjectFortress/tests/Name.fss`, whose component is `Name`.

- Every `.fss` file there is gated, with no `.test` file needed.
- It is green if it throws no exception, exits 0, and neither its standard output nor its standard error contains `fail` or `FAIL`. A longer word counts too: `failure` fails the test. Only a file whose name contains `QuickCheckTest` is exempt.
- An api that it imports, and a helper component, go in `ProjectFortress/test_library/`. In `tests/`, a helper would run as a test.
- The harness skips files whose names end in `Syntax.fss`, `DynamicSemantics.fss` or `Satisfiability.fss`, or contain `GenomeUtil`.
- For a refusal at load, put `Name.test` beside `tests/Name.fss`, with `load_exception_contains=<message>`. A plain test is green if walk refuses the program at load as named. A failure while the top-level variables are initialised counts as a refusal. An `XXX` test with such a `.test` file is green if the program loads and runs clean.

Compiled: write `Name.fss` and `Name.test` in the compiled test folder that holds tests of its kind:

- `library_tests/`: the compiler's library. A test of the interpreter's library is an interpreter test (above).
- `parser_tests/`: the parser.
- `compiler_tests/`: the rest, beside the team's numbered `CompiledN` tests.
- `other_compiler_tests/`: the team's compiled tests that do not fit the `CompiledN` series, by the comment in `OtherCompilerJUTest.java`. Put no new test there.

The `.test` files are the whole list of tests: a `.fss` that no `.test` file names never runs. A `.test` file is a Java property file. It names the commands to run and the checks on their output, as lit's RUN and CHECK lines do:

    tests=Name                 the component(s) it drives; without it, the .test file's own name
    compile | link | typecheck each present command is one JUnit case; link compiles, then links
    run                        run the linked program in a subprocess (bin/fortress run)
    <command>_<stream>_<check>=text
                               command: compile, link or run; stream: out, err or exception;
                               check: contains, does_not_contain, equals, matches,
                               WIcontains (containment with runs of whitespace collapsed)

A `run` fails if the program exits non-zero or a `run_*` check fails. With no `run_out` check, its output must contain `pass` or `PASS`. With `run_exits_nonzero=true`, the run must exit non-zero, as a program whose class fails to load does. The `run_*` checks, and the `PASS` check where no `run_out` check is given, still apply. For example:

    tests=EqualityRung1
    link
    run
    run_out_WIcontains=PASS

## How `XXX` works

- Under walk, an `XXX` test is `tests/XXXName.fss`, whose component is `XXXName`. With no `.test` file, it is green when it fails as a plain test would.

- The harness reports any link or compile exception of a component whose name contains `XXX` as expected, whatever the `.test` file's name. Only an unmet key of that command makes it red.
- An `XXX` compile test with a `compile_err_contains` key, whose program compiles, reports "Saw wrong failure", which is red.
- A green `XXX` test prints `Saw expected failure` or `OK Saw expected exception`.

## How a defect is recorded

Record every defect that you measure in one of three ways, and say in your report which:

1. Your change repairs it: an assertion in your plain gated test. It needs no `XXX` stage.
2. It is deferred, and the specification settles it: a gated `XXX` test that asserts the specification's answer. Write it in the change that measured the defect, even if a later change will repair it. If walk crashes on the program, still write the `XXX` test, unlike under 3: the harness counts the crash as the expected failure. A deferred defect of a program that the checker accepts and that then fails the JVM's verification (`VerifyError`), linkage or a range check at run time is one of these.
3. It is deferred, and the specification is silent or a conflict leaves it open (`exploring.md`): a test that asserts today's behaviour, and a row in the gap ledger (`records.md`). If no program can observe the defect, or no gated test can pass while it shows, as when walk crashes on the program, write the ledger row only. Its reproducer, the row's cell that names the test, is `none`, and its notes give the command and its output.

If your brief does not let you edit the original tree, say in your report which of the three the defect needs, and write a ledger row for it, whichever it needs. A probe that only measures and reports is an example. The change that next works there writes the test.

Under walk, do it before you edit a library source that the test reads. If your tree already holds the fix, run the test through the harness on the old code, as `worktrees.md`, "Running the old code", says.
3. Make the fix. See the test pass in your last run after your last change of code.

The test needs no commit of its own. A test that comes with no fix, such as one that guards a behaviour that works today, has no failing run: see it pass through the harness.

Assert a value with `assert` in an interpreter test. In a compiled test, assert it with `assert` (above), or print it and check it with a `run_out_equals` key. The harness checks both, so they are part of the suite's verdict.

## Writing an `XXX` test

- For a refusal at compile time, write one `XXX` compile test, with `compile` and `compile_err_contains=<the refusal's message>`.

  - `XXXName.test`, with `tests=XXXName` and `run`, and no `link`. Its run uses the plain file's link, so run the two files in one call of `junit.sh` or `fortress junit`, the plain one first.
  - The program prints `REACHED` in `run()` before the part that fails. The `XXX` file checks it with `run_out_contains=REACHED`, or with `run_out_does_not_contain=REACHED` if the run dies before `run()` prints. Never use `run_out_contains=PASS`.
  - Example: `compiler_tests/XXXBoxDotSpellingsRungW.test` and `BoxDotSpellingsRungWLink.test`.

Show the first `XXX` test that your change adds, and only the first, working through the harness (`harness-one.sh`, `junit.sh` or `fortress junit`), from its place in a gated test folder. A direct compile and run does not show this. Run it twice:

1	# The library
2	
3	The library is `Library/` and `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/`, without the compiler's own files there:
4	
5	- In `Library/`: the interpreter's prelude, `FortressLibrary.fss` and `.fsi`, and its other components. The compiler's `CompilerLibrary`, `CompilerAlgebra` and `CompilerSystem` are not part of it. `FortressAst.fss` and `.fsi` are generated from `ProjectFortress/astgen/Fortress.ast`: edit that file, never these two.
6	- In `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/`: `FortressBuiltin`, `NativeArray` and the rest. The compiler's `CompilerBuiltin` is not part of it.
7	- `LibraryBuiltin/AnyType`, the top type, belongs to both libraries. After an edit to it, also take the compiled path's step (`build-and-caches.md`, "After an edit of the library").
8	- `Library/incomplete/` is not on the source path (`default_repository/configuration`), so no program can import what it declares. Nothing that the suites or the model program run imports `Library/GeneratorLibrary.fss` either. Before you cite a declaration as the library's way, check that a running program can reach it.
9	
10	## How loops and reductions call the library
11	
12	The desugarer, which both paths share, turns these forms into calls of the library:
13	
14	- `for x <- g do b end` becomes `g.loop(fn x => b)`, a call of the generator's `loop` method. Each further generator nests one more `loop` call inside.
15	- `while x <- e do b end` becomes `while __whileCond(e, fn x => b) do end`. `if x <- e then ... end` becomes a call of `__cond`.
16	- A comprehension or a big operator, such as `SUM`, becomes a call of `__bigOperator`, whose argument calls `__generate` on each generator. So does a big operator inside another: no desugaring calls the library's `__bigOperator2`.
17	
18	These functions work on the library's generators and reductions: `trait Generator` and `trait Reduction` in `FortressLibrary.fsi`, and `RangeInternals.fss` for ranges. `FortressLibrary.fss` also defines `__loop`, but no desugaring calls it. So a failure inside a loop or a reduction is most often in the library's code, and its fix is a library edit.
19	
20	## The curator's decisions on the library
21	
22	- Scalar ranges are over `ZZ32` only. A range over another integer type is a static error, and walk stops when it builds one. Write a wider counter as a `ZZ32` loop that widens its index.
23	- `ZZ32` and numerals convert into `RR64` implicitly. `ZZ64` converts into `RR64` only explicitly, by `asFloat`.
24	- For arithmetic that wraps on overflow, use the wrapping operators ∔ `DOTPLUS`, ∸ `DOTMINUS` and ⨰ `DOTTIMES`. Parenthesise every such expression fully, because their precedence is stated only among themselves.
25	- `SUM` and `PROD` are generic over `AdditiveGroup` and `MultiplicativeRing`. The element type is written before the generators, as in `SUM[\ZZ32\][j <- 0#n] f(j)`. In the library, write it, as its own sites do. For a call without it, the checker takes the reduction's expected type, or else its body's type (`revival-changes.md`, "Reductions and comprehensions"). Walk runs such a call at its value's declared type, or else at the join of its elements' run-time types. An empty `SUM` with no static argument written and no declared type gives the integer 0, and an empty `PROD` the integer 1, whatever the body's type (ledger row 716). With a static argument written that is not a number type, such as a user group, an empty or filtered `SUM` ends in `CastError` (ledger row 436).
26	- An indexed type's index parameter is bounded by `Index` (`revival-changes.md`, "Traits and objects"). `BoundedRange[\I\]` cannot take the bound, because the open range `(:)` stays a range over `Any` (P-56). So its `atMost(n: I): FullRange[\I\]` has the condition `where { I extends Index }`, which each call must meet (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi`). A type whose static parameter is a range's index type takes the bound too, as `UniformDistribution[\T extends Index\]` over a `FullRange[\T\]` (`Library/Random.fsi`).
27	- An array's `fill` takes a value, and its `tabulate` a function of the index: `array[\ZZ32\](4).fill(0)`, `array[\ZZ32\](4).tabulate(fn (i:ZZ32):ZZ32 => 10 i)`. The factories that take a function are `tabulatedArray1` to `tabulatedArray3` and `tabulatedVector`.
28	
29	## Designing a change
30	
31	- Put each extension into this library, outside the compiler's files. This includes an extension that only the model program needs.
32	- Fix a gap in the library, not by a workaround in the program that meets it. Take the design from the library's practice as well as from the specification's text. If the two disagree, do as `specification.md`, "When the text and an implementation disagree", says.
33	- If a rule of the language or the checker refuses the way that you want, find how the library writes that kind of thing. Do the same. The checker's refusals of this library reach you through your brief, or through a run of the count stage (`compiler.md`): `fortress typecheck` checks against the compiler's prelude.
34	- When you add a method, make it dotted or functional as its family in the library does. If the family shows no practice, follow the team's proposal, which no program can import (`Library/incomplete/Collection.fss`): an updater, a getter or a setter, indexing included, is dotted, and every other method is functional.
35	- A new functional method reserves its name in every program that imports the library. The phase that binds names then refuses each program that names a variable or a parameter after it: "Variable even is already declared."

# The library

The library is `Library/` and `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/`, without the compiler's own files there:

- In `Library/`: the interpreter's prelude, `FortressLibrary.fss` and `.fsi`, and its other components. The compiler's `CompilerLibrary`, `CompilerAlgebra` and `CompilerSystem` are not part of it. `FortressAst.fss` and `.fsi` are generated from `ProjectFortress/astgen/Fortress.ast`: edit that file, never these two.
- In `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/`: `FortressBuiltin`, `NativeArray` and the rest. The compiler's `CompilerBuiltin` is not part of it.
- `LibraryBuiltin/AnyType`, the top type, belongs to both libraries. After an edit to it, also take the compiled path's step (`build-and-caches.md`, "After an edit of the library").
- `Library/incomplete/` is not on the source path (`default_repository/configuration`), so no program can import what it declares. Nothing that the suites or the model program run imports `Library/GeneratorLibrary.fss` either. Before you cite a declaration as the library's way, check that a running program can reach it.

## How loops and reductions call the library

The desugarer, which both paths share, turns these forms into calls of the library:

- `for x <- g do b end` becomes `g.loop(fn x => b)`, a call of the generator's `loop` method. Each further generator nests one more `loop` call inside.
- `while x <- e do b end` becomes `while __whileCond(e, fn x => b) do end`. `if x <- e then ... end` becomes a call of `__cond`.
- A comprehension or a big operator, such as `SUM`, becomes a call of `__bigOperator`, whose argument calls `__generate` on each generator. So does a big operator inside another: no desugaring calls the library's `__bigOperator2`.

These functions work on the library's generators and reductions: `trait Generator` and `trait Reduction` in `FortressLibrary.fsi`, and `RangeInternals.fss` for ranges. `FortressLibrary.fss` also defines `__loop`, but no desugaring calls it. So a failure inside a loop or a reduction is most often in the library's code, and its fix is a library edit.

## The curator's decisions on the library

- Scalar ranges are over `ZZ32` only. A range over another integer type is a static error, and walk stops when it builds one. Write a wider counter as a `ZZ32` loop that widens its index.
- `ZZ32` and numerals convert into `RR64` implicitly. `ZZ64` converts into `RR64` only explicitly, by `asFloat`.
- For arithmetic that wraps on overflow, use the wrapping operators ∔ `DOTPLUS`, ∸ `DOTMINUS` and ⨰ `DOTTIMES`. Parenthesise every such expression fully, because their precedence is stated only among themselves.
- `SUM` and `PROD` are generic over `AdditiveGroup` and `MultiplicativeRing`. The element type is written before the generators, as in `SUM[\ZZ32\][j <- 0#n] f(j)`. In the library, write it, as its own sites do. For a call without it, the checker takes the reduction's expected type, or else its body's type (`revival-changes.md`, "Reductions and comprehensions"). Walk runs such a call at its value's declared type, or else at the join of its elements' run-time types. An empty `SUM` with no static argument written and no declared type gives the integer 0, and an empty `PROD` the integer 1, whatever the body's type (ledger row 716). With a static argument written that is not a number type, such as a user group, an empty or filtered `SUM` ends in `CastError` (ledger row 436).
- An indexed type's index parameter is bounded by `Index` (`revival-changes.md`, "Traits and objects"). `BoundedRange[\I\]` cannot take the bound, because the open range `(:)` stays a range over `Any` (P-56). So its `atMost(n: I): FullRange[\I\]` has the condition `where { I extends Index }`, which each call must meet (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi`). A type whose static parameter is a range's index type takes the bound too, as `UniformDistribution[\T extends Index\]` over a `FullRange[\T\]` (`Library/Random.fsi`).
- An array's `fill` takes a value, and its `tabulate` a function of the index: `array[\ZZ32\](4).fill(0)`, `array[\ZZ32\](4).tabulate(fn (i:ZZ32):ZZ32 => 10 i)`. The factories that take a function are `tabulatedArray1` to `tabulatedArray3` and `tabulatedVector`.

## Designing a change

- Put each extension into this library, outside the compiler's files. This includes an extension that only the model program needs.
- Fix a gap in the library, not by a workaround in the program that meets it. Take the design from the library's practice as well as from the specification's text. If the two disagree, do as `specification.md`, "When the text and an implementation disagree", says.
- If a rule of the language or the checker refuses the way that you want, find how the library writes that kind of thing. Do the same. The checker's refusals of this library reach you through your brief, or through a run of the count stage (`compiler.md`): `fortress typecheck` checks against the compiler's prelude.
- When you add a method, make it dotted or functional as its family in the library does. If the family shows no practice, follow the team's proposal, which no program can import (`Library/incomplete/Collection.fss`): an updater, a getter or a setter, indexing included, is dotted, and every other method is functional.
- A new functional method reserves its name in every program that imports the library. The phase that binds names then refuses each program that names a variable or a parameter after it: "Variable even is already declared."
- A `fail` without a static argument has the result type `Any`. Where it must have a type, write the static argument, as `strToInt` calls `fail[\ZZ32\]`.
- A dotted method shadows a top-level function of the same name (`overloading.tex`, "Principles of Overloading").
- In an api, declare each top-level function and each member of a trait or object at the header that the component gives it. A function's header is its name, its static parameters with their bounds, its modifiers, its `throws` clause, its parameters' modifiers and types, and its return type. A function's parameters' names and a `where` clause do not count, but each static parameter's name counts (ledger row 836). Give an object's value parameters the api's names, because they are its fields (`compiler.md`, "Traps of the compiled path"). In the cases below, change the component's header to the api's, not the api's to the component's. The examples are in `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi` and `Library/FortressLibrary.fss`.
  - The member's body already answers the api's type. `RR64`'s `opr |\self/|`, `opr |/self\|` and `truncate` answer `ZZ64`, because they call `Float`'s natives, which answer `ZZ64` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:184-191`).
  - The api cannot name the component's type. `Array2`'s and `Array3`'s `bounds` and `zeroIndices` answered types of `RangeInternals`, which depends on this api. They now answer the api's `CompactFullRange` types, which those types extend.
  - The api's type is wider, and the overrides and bodies use only that type. `DelegatedIndexed`'s `generator` answers the api's `Generator[\E\]`, as `FlatString`'s override does.

  In the api, write `abstract` on each member that the component leaves without a body.
- The compiled checker's export check matches each api member with a component member of the same name and header. It matches these members in these ways:
  - A field, as `x: ZZ32` in an api's trait: by a component field of its name, its type and its modifiers other than `var`. A component's getter does not match it, so declare a field in the component too (ledger row 842).
  - An object's value parameter: by its type and its modifiers other than `var`, but not by its name.
  - A getter written `abstract`, as `abstract getter one(): T`: by a component getter at its header, or by a component field of its name and type that is neither `hidden` nor `private`. A `hidden` field has no getter.
  - Another member written `abstract`: by a component member at the api's header, with a body or without one.

  Each entry of the check's error names a trait or object and only its first member that differs. After you fix that member, check again to see the next. These steps run the check:
  - For a component of a compiled program or test: `fortress compile`.
  - For the one library's `FortressLibrary` component: the count stage (`compiler.md`, "The checker's time").
  - For the other thirteen components that the gate's distance stage checks: that stage. When a rung needs it, the brief gives its command.
  - For another component of the one library: no step, until the switch-over.
- A new overload can make walk refuse every program at load. `interpreter.md`, "What walk checks", lists what walk refuses.
- Write a new native as a public static method of a class under `nativeHelpers/`, and bind it with `builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.Class.method")`. Both paths run it. Give it the Java types that carry the declared types (`interpreter.md`, "Natives"). Write a glue class under `interpreter/glue/prim/`, which only walk runs, only where no Java type carries a declared type, as for the bindings in `Library/Reflect.fss`. A native is an edit of Java: rebuild (`build-and-caches.md`, "Two layers of code"), and test it on both paths (`compiler.md`, "Natives").
- `interpreter.md`, "The model program", says how to check microGPT under walk.

## Editing

A comment after a declaration that ends in an expression or a type becomes part of that declaration's source span. It also becomes part of the unambiguous name made from the span. So a comment-only edit changes the syntax tree. Before you compare parse trees or diagnostics across such an edit, map their positions back to the lines before the edit. Three removed scripts did this: `parse-compare.sh`, `ast-compare.py` and `remap-lines.py`. Print one with `git show ab067d9b6^:explorations/compile-ladder/rung-library-comments/<name>`.

content.content:
.claude/skills/fortress-repo/references/revival-changes.md:7:A sentence that cites a ledger row states a behaviour that is not settled: a known departure from a rule, or a case that the rules do not decide yet. Either can change, so do not assert it as correct in a plain test, one without the `XXX` prefix (`tests-writing.md`). A sentence that opens "Until the switch-over" states a limit of the compiler's library. The limit ends when the compiled path moves onto the interpreter's library, so do not fix it in the compiler's prelude (`compiler.md`). If a change is not here, search FACTS and POSITIONS (`records.md`) before you call a disagreement a conflict. An old note, a team test and your training can be right about the team's walk and wrong here: the number types do not nest, fixed-width arithmetic does not wrap, and walk converts arguments.
.claude/skills/fortress-repo/references/revival-changes.md:60:- a value object is equivalent field by field, a tuple element by element, an integer, a character or a boolean by its value, and a float by its bits;
.claude/skills/fortress-repo/references/revival-changes.md:64:So for a value object `V` without its own `=`, `V(s) = V(t)` is `false` where `s` and `t` are equal strings made by two computations. Two string literals of one text are one object (P-171). So `"ab" SEQV "ab"` and `V("ab") = V("ab")` are `true`. Two string literals joined by `||` fold into one ("Numbers"), so `("a" || "b") SEQV "ab"` is `true`. A float numeral converts where `RR64` is declared ("Numbers"), so `y: RR64 = 0.5` is `SEQV` a computed `RR64` 0.5. The interpreter's library declares `=` on pairs and triples only, so `(s, 1, 2, 3) = (t, 1, 2, 3)` falls back to `SEQV` and is `false`; row 923 holds the question of longer tuples. To compare by content, give the value object an `=`, or compare the parts. A string's `=` compares text. Until the switch-over, the compiler's library declares no `=` over `Any` and none on tuples. Its own `≣`, declared as `===`, compares strings and `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `RR32` and `RR64` by `=`, not by bits or identity (row 908).
.claude/skills/fortress-repo/references/revival-changes.md:89:**The number types are flat siblings (P-43).** The record calls this choice route A. It still calls the number and order traits "the tower", which does not mean that they nest.
.claude/skills/fortress-repo/references/revival-changes.md:91:**A numeral converts where it stands (P-173).** A numeral's own type is `NaturalNumeral[\n, r, v\]`, or `RadixPointNumeral[\n, m, r, v\]` with a radix point (P-174). Its static arguments are the numeral's numbers: `n` the digit count, `m` the count of digits after the point, `r` the radix, and `v` the digits read as one integer in that radix, so `3.125` is a `RadixPointNumeral[\4, 3, 10, 3125\]`. Both lie below `Numeral`, a sibling of the number types under `Number`. No numeral value exists when a program runs, so a numeral type has no getters, no `asFloat`, no `asString` and no `=` with a number type. Until the switch-over, the compiler's prelude follows the same design (P-37).
.claude/skills/fortress-repo/references/revival-changes.md:93:A place fixes a type when its declared type has a coercion from the numeral type, as each of the eight number types has. Such places are a typed binding, an assignment, a field, a parameter and a declared return type. At a number type, the numeral converts from its exact value: exactly into the five integer types and `QQ`, and with one rounding into `RR64` and `RR32` (P-76, P-172). So `u: NN32 = 5` binds, and `q: QQ = 0.1` is `1/10`. A numeral outside the type's range, or that rounds to an infinity there, is refused: by the checker statically, by walk when the place runs. Walk's message depends on the place: a top-level binding gives 'Type mismatch binding', a parameter 'got arg'. # Committing and pushing

**scratch**
: Files and folders that your work makes and `main` does not keep: logs, captured and raw run output, copies of tools, probe programs, lists and private caches folders.

Your brief says whether you commit and push, and on which branch. If it says nothing, commit on your current branch, and push it.

## What to commit

- Commit your change, its tests, your report if it is a file, and any reusable script.
- Commit what you write to the record, such as a ledger row, with the work that it records. A row's close follows the fix's commit (`records.md`).
- Keep scratch in your tree's `tmp/`, which is gitignored.
- In a fresh clone, `.claude/worktrees/` and `.claude/agents/` show as untracked, because the lines of `.git/info/exclude` that hide them are not in the clone. Do not commit them.
- Keep a copyrighted PDF or deck in `research/decks/`, which is gitignored. Cite it by its Wayback URL. Notes on it go in `research/extracts/`: your own summary, with brief attributed quotations.
- Put provenance and rationale in commit messages and reports, not in source comments.
- Name a model by its tier (Opus, Sonnet, Fable) in any text that you commit, commit messages included. Never write its model identifier, the API's name for the model, which starts with `claude-`.

## How to commit

Commit as you go, each commit in one command that names its paths:

    git add -- <paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <paths>

- The command commits only the paths that it names. Other agents may have uncommitted edits in your tree. Leave them alone.
- If you renamed a file with `git mv`, name its old path in `git commit` only, because `git add` refuses a path that no longer exists: `git add -- <new paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <new paths> <old paths>`.
- Never commit a copied directory, and never use `git add -A`.
- Before you commit more than a few hundred lines, stage them and read what you staged: `git add -- <paths> && git diff --cached --stat -- <paths>`.
- If the commit edits the original tree, say so in its message.
- End every commit message with this footer, exactly, whatever footer Claude Code suggests:

      Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
      Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AmiXNpJxQ6TBwec4vJZHDB

  If your brief gives another session line, use it. If a commit that is already made has a footer that names a model, by any name or identifier, leave the commit as it is. Such a footer is not a defect: do not check for it, report it or list it.

## Pushing

Push after every commit, so that a lost container loses nothing.

- If you work on your own branch, push it: `git push -u origin <branch>` the first time, then `git push`. Your brief says how the branch reaches `main`.
- From a session in a cloud container, do not try to delete a branch on GitHub, or retry a refusal with another tool (the `cloud-container` skill, "Rules for every agent"). Removing a worktree does not delete its branch, which stays. Ask nobody in your report to delete a branch.
- If you work on `main`, other agents commit to it too. Push only your own commits:
  1. Run `git log origin/main..main`. Your commits are those whose hashes your own `git commit` printed.
  2. If it lists another agent's commit, run the command again shortly: that agent pushes right after it commits. If the commit stays, push nothing, and say so in your report.
  3. If it lists only your commits, push the three refs with this one command, and wait for it to end:

         git push --atomic origin main main:claude/worker-brief-fable-vnnuv8 main:blinded-fable

     With `--atomic`, the three refs update together or not at all. Do not pipe the command into another command, since a pipe hides a refusal. A refusal shows as a line that starts with `!`, and as a non-zero exit. The last ref keeps `blinded-fable` current. If the container is lost, the platform rebuilds it from that branch.
- Push no branch that this section does not name, unless your brief names it.
- If a push is refused, push nothing more, and do not run it again. Report the refused ref and git's message.

# Committing and pushing

**scratch**
: Files and folders that your work makes and `main` does not keep: logs, captured and raw run output, copies of tools, lists and private caches folders.

Your brief says whether you commit and push, and on which branch. If it says nothing, commit on your current branch, and push it.

## What to commit

- Commit your change, its tests, your report if it is a file, and any reusable script.
- Commit what you write to the record, such as a ledger row, with the work that it records. A row's close follows the fix's commit (`records.md`).
- A probe builds a change to answer a question, and does not land it. Commit its patch, its report and its programs in the `probes/` folder that your brief names. Its code reaches `main` only when a later change lands it, test first.
- Keep scratch in your tree's `tmp/`, which is gitignored.
- Do not commit `.claude/worktrees/` or `.claude/agents/`, which show as untracked in a fresh clone.
- Keep a copyrighted PDF or deck in `research/decks/`, which is gitignored. Cite it by its Wayback URL. Notes on it go in `research/extracts/`: your own summary, with brief attributed quotations.
- Put provenance and rationale in commit messages and reports, not in source comments.
- Name a model by its tier (Opus, Sonnet, Fable) in any text that you commit, commit messages included. Never write its model identifier, the API's name for the model, which starts with `claude-`.

## How to commit

Commit as you go, each commit in one command that names its paths:

    git add -- <paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <paths>

- The command commits only the paths that it names. Other agents may have uncommitted edits in your tree. Leave them alone.
- If you renamed a file with `git mv`, name its old path in `git commit` only, because `git add` refuses a path that no longer exists: `git add -- <new paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <new paths> <old paths>`.
- Never commit a copied directory, and never use `git add -A`.
- Before you commit more than a few hundred lines, stage them and read what you staged: `git add -- <paths> && git diff --cached --stat -- <paths>`.
- If the commit edits the original tree, say so in its message.
- End every commit message with this footer, exactly, whatever footer Claude Code suggests:

      Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
      Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AmiXNpJxQ6TBwec4vJZHDB

  If your brief gives another session line, use it. If a commit that is already made has a footer that names a model, by any name or identifier, leave the commit as it is. Such a footer is not a defect: do not check for it, report it or list it.

## Pushing

Push after every commit, so that a lost container loses nothing.

- If you work on your own branch, push it: `git push -u origin <branch>` the first time, then `git push`. Your brief says how the branch reaches `main`.
- From a session in a cloud container, do not try to delete a branch on GitHub, or retry a refusal with another tool (the `cloud-container` skill, "Rules for every agent"). Removing a worktree does not delete its branch, which stays. Ask nobody in your report to delete a branch.
- If you work on `main`, other agents commit to it too. Push only your own commits:
  1. Run `git log origin/main..main`. Your commits are those whose hashes your own `git commit` printed.
  2. If it lists another agent's commit, run the command again shortly: that agent pushes right after it commits. If the commit stays, push nothing, and say so in your report.
  3. If it lists only your commits, push the three refs with this one command, and wait for it to end:

         git push --atomic origin main main:claude/worker-brief-fable-vnnuv8 main:blinded-fable

     With `--atomic`, the three refs update together or not at all. Do not pipe the command into another command, since a pipe hides a refusal. A refusal shows as a line that starts with `!`, and as a non-zero exit. The last ref keeps `blinded-fable` current. If the container is lost, the platform rebuilds it from that branch.
- Push no branch that this section does not name, unless your brief names it.
- If a push is refused, push nothing more, and do not run it again. Report the refused ref and git's message.

# Exploring: a question that the record does not settle

The record keeps what earlier workers found, and they met many of the same questions. Workers have called a thing absent or new when the record already held it.

## The choices that are yours

The curator settles every conflict and every question about a decision of the curator. Any other choice is yours only if it meets all four of these conditions:

- It changes only one area.
- It changes no line of the model program.
- It changes no decision of the curator.
- It can be undone.

## Weighing the sources

The type group is the part of the team that built the type checker and the compiler, from 2009 to 2012. Where their late positions disagree with the specification's earlier text, the late positions weigh more. These positions are:

- the exclusion rule;
- compiled code specialised to each instantiation of a generic, which they kept;
- the compiled number tower, which they flattened in 2009 and 2010;
- the 2012 write-up on the Return Type Rule (`Papers/Types/journal/`);
- the POPL 2019 paper on symmetric multiple dispatch (`research/extracts/ParkPOPL2019-extract.md`).

The team's later work is outside the original tree. It is in these places:

- `research/extracts/`: the POPL 2019 paper, Steele's talks of 2015 and 2016, and the project's web sites with the post of July 2012 that ended the project;
- the reading of the team's 2012 patents: `explorations/reviews/mie-probes/patents-forest-rule.md`.

If a conflict or a decision not taken needs the designers' reason for a rule, print the row of its design area. WORD is a word of the area, such as `coercion`, `juxtaposition`, `dispatch` or `Arrays`. A word can match several rows, each about 1 to 2 KB.

    explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh 'map:design-intent-sources.md#The map, by design area@WORD'

Then open the sources that the row names. Among them are the `\note{}` boxes and the team's written rationale in the Internal Document appendix: `Specification/appendices/FAQ.tex` and `future.tex`. The row also names the later works that speak to its area, after the words "after the repository (§7)". To read what one of them covers and does not cover, print its row of the map's section "After the repository". WORD is a word of its title, such as `Polymorphic`, `patents`, `JuliaCon` or `Wrapping`. A row is about 1 to 2 KB.

    explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh 'map:design-intent-sources.md#After the repository@WORD'

When your report describes the team's sources on a question, say which of them is one of the late positions above. If the question is about a type rule, also name each later work that you checked.

## The procedure

1. Search the record with the queries in `records.md`. If two of the team's sources disagree, look for the construct in `revival-changes.md` before you search the record.
2. If the record or `revival-changes.md` settles the question, go back to building. Cite what settles it.

# Committing and pushing

**scratch**
: Files and folders that your work makes and `main` does not keep: logs, captured and raw run output, copies of tools, lists and private caches folders.

Your brief says whether you commit and push, and on which branch. If it says nothing, commit on your current branch, and push it.

## What to commit

- Commit your change, its tests, your report if it is a file, and any reusable script.
- Commit what you write to the record, such as a ledger row, with the work that it records. A row's close follows the fix's commit (`records.md`).
- A probe builds a change to answer a question, and does not land it. Commit its patch, its report and its programs in the `probes/` folder that your brief names. Its code reaches `main` only when a later change lands it, test first.
- Keep scratch in your tree's `tmp/`, which is gitignored.
- Do not commit `.claude/worktrees/` or `.claude/agents/`, which show as untracked in a fresh clone.
- Keep a copyrighted PDF or deck in `research/decks/`, which is gitignored. Cite it by its Wayback URL. Notes on it go in `research/extracts/`: your own summary, with brief attributed quotations.
- Put provenance and rationale in commit messages and reports, not in source comments.
- Name a model by its tier (Opus, Sonnet, Fable) in any text that you commit, commit messages included. Never write its model identifier, the API's name for the model, which starts with `claude-`.

## How to commit

Commit as you go, each commit in one command that names its paths:

    git add -- <paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <paths>

- The command commits only the paths that it names. Other agents may have uncommitted edits in your tree. Leave them alone.
- If you renamed a file with `git mv`, name its old path in `git commit` only, because `git add` refuses a path that no longer exists: `git add -- <new paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <new paths> <old paths>`.
- Never commit a copied directory, and never use `git add -A`.
- Before you commit more than a few hundred lines, stage them and read what you staged: `git add -- <paths> && git diff --cached --stat -- <paths>`.
- If the commit edits the original tree, say so in its message.
- End every commit message with this footer, exactly, whatever footer Claude Code suggests:

      Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
      Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AmiXNpJxQ6TBwec4vJZHDB

  If your brief gives another session line, use it. If a commit that is already made has a footer that names a model, by any name or identifier, leave the commit as it is. Such a footer is not a defect: do not check for it, report it or list it.

## Pushing

Push after every commit, so that a lost container loses nothing.

- If you work on your own branch, push it: `git push -u origin <branch>` the first time, then `git push`. Your brief says how the branch reaches `main`.
- From a session in a cloud container, do not try to delete a branch on GitHub, or retry a refusal with another tool (the `cloud-container` skill, "Rules for every agent"). Removing a worktree does not delete its branch, which stays. Ask nobody in your report to delete a branch.
- If you work on `main`, other agents commit to it too. Push only your own commits:
  1. Run `git log origin/main..main`. Your commits are those whose hashes your own `git commit` printed.
  2. If it lists another agent's commit, run the command again shortly: that agent pushes right after it commits. If the commit stays, push nothing, and say so in your report.
  3. If it lists only your commits, push the three refs with this one command, and wait for it to end:

         git push --atomic origin main main:claude/worker-brief-fable-vnnuv8 main:blinded-fable

     With `--atomic`, the three refs update together or not at all. Do not pipe the command into another command, since a pipe hides a refusal. A refusal shows as a line that starts with `!`, and as a non-zero exit. The platform rebuilds a lost container from `blinded-fable`.
- Push no branch that this section does not name, unless your brief names it.
- If a push is refused, push nothing more, and do not run it again. Report the refused ref and git's message.
